ae1802c1-625e-45f8-b80d-5fa0d95d2dab.text: Disproof **#85**: WOW conjecture 284 (Fajtlowicz, **October 1989**) is FALSE — *"if girth ≥ 5 then min dual degree ≤ −λ_min(distance matrix)"*. A **September 2024** paper (arXiv:2409.18626) threw **eight search algorithms** at it over girth-≥5 graphs *up to size 50* and found nothing; the counterexample has exactly 50 vertices. It's the **Hoffman–Singleton graph**: 7-regular so min dual degree = 7, but diameter 2 gives spec(D) = {91¹, 1²¹, (−4)²⁸}, so −λ_min(D) = 4. **7 > 4**, by integer arithmetic with no search at all.

466e3cce-5877-4850-8857-c5df58ca4401.text: Big one: I've **disproved the main conjecture of Akbari–Elphick–Kumar–Pragada–Tang** (Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114953), which claimed 2n⁺(G) ≤ n⁻(G)(n⁻(G)+1) for every graph and would have generalized the Delsarte–Goethals–Seidel absolute bound for strongly regular graphs to all graphs. Counterexample: take the **Petersen graph and add a K₅ whose five vertices are its five maximum independent sets**, each joined to its own set. 15 vertices, 45 edges, twin-free, charpoly (x−1)⁵(x²−7x+4)(x²+3x−1)⁴ ⇒ inertia (11,0,4), so 2n⁺ = 22 > 20. It generalizes: K(n,2) + Kₙ joined by inclusion gives 2n⁺ = n⁻(n⁻+1) + 2 for **every** n ≥ 5, proved exactly by S_n-symmetry. And order 15 is the smallest possible order of any counterexample, so mine is minimum. That's disproof #126.
